summary: The note describes how public health officials are using innovative outreach to fight the tobacco epidemic, which causes over 7 million deaths globally each year. It covers smartphone apps, influencer partnerships, local city programs, storytelling campaigns, activism against industry tactics, healthcare provider toolkits, and social impact bonds for financing. Quotes from experts and participants illustrate each approach, and the note ends with an optimistic vision of a tobacco-free future.
one_line: Public health groups are fighting tobacco with apps, influencers, local programs, storytelling, provider toolkits, and social impact bond financing.
key_facts: The CDC says tobacco use is the single largest preventable cause of death and illness in the world, causing more than 7 million deaths globally each year.
Dr. Angela Patterson, Chief Medical Officer at the CDC, said on September 5, 2023 that innovative outreach is crucial in addressing the complex factors behind tobacco use.
Health departments have started rolling out quit-smoking apps offering cigarette-free day tracking, health improvement timelines, and gamified rewards.
Dr. Jason Hargrove commented on October 10, 2023 that meeting smokers on their phones personalizes the quit experience and can increase cessation success.
Influencer Vanessa Lopes said on November 2, 2023 that the goal is 'making not smoking cool again'.
On December 15, 2023, the city of Springfield unveiled a community engagement program spearheaded by Mayor Thomas Kincaid, involving health workers, schools, and businesses.
The 'Real Stories' campaign, started in January 2024, profiles former smokers and their journeys to a tobacco-free life; Michael Thompson is a participant.
Emily Sanchez, a health policy expert, spoke at a forum on February 3, 2024 about countering tobacco industry misinformation and manipulation tactics.
The American Medical Association launched a toolkit on March 1, 2024 for providers across the country to support patients in quitting.
Dr. Olivia Roberts, a family physician, said trust-based patient relationships make provider advice about quitting a powerful motivator.
Some states are experimenting with social impact bonds, which channel private investment to public health campaigns with returns linked to reduced smoking rates.
Economic analyst Mark Franklin explained on April 10, 2024 that social impact bonds create win-win situations.
